name: Beechcraft Duchess (76)
summary: Four-seat twin trainer built 1978–1983 from Musketeer-family components, recognizable by its T-tail and counter-rotating engines.

wings: Low, straight wing with rounded tips
engines: Two small Lycoming engines in compact nacelles
tail: T-tail: horizontal stabilizer on top of a swept fin

tellTales: Small low-wing twin with a T-tail
Rounded four-seat cabin with a smooth nose
Compact engine nacelles on a straight wing

confusedWith.howToTell: Both are T-tail four-seat twins; the Duchess has a rounder Beech-style cabin and smooth nose, while the Seminole's cabin is boxier and PA-28 derived.
The Seneca has a conventional low tail and a longer six-seat cabin; the Duchess has a T-tail and a shorter cabin.
The DA42 is a smooth composite twin with long slender wings and winglets; the Duchess is a metal twin with a short, straight wing.
